title: Privacy-safe support and migration tooling
summary: Diagnostics are now package-aware: the support bundle reports package version, model state (loaded/valid/missing), service state (socket active/inactive), protection state (TPM/software), enabled PAM service count, installed split packages (namtor/namtor-gnome/namtor-kde), and migration artifacts from prior manual/monolithic installs — all without exposing file paths, boot IDs, model hashes (full), thresholds, scores, embeddings, gate names, raw logs, template paths, or key paths. Long hex IDs are redacted to first 8 chars + '...'. The privacy scanner forbidden terms were extended from 7 to 11 (added score, biometric, gate, raw). The log filter terms were extended from 9 to 13 (added key, path, gate, raw). The bundle README text was rewritten to avoid forbidden terms. Migration detection checks for legacy setuid helper (namtor-worker-spawn), legacy install script, and manual install without manifest.

fields_reported: enabled PAM service count (files in /etc/pam.d containing pam_namtor.so)
fields_never_reported: model hashes (full — redacted to first 8 chars)

privacy_scanner.hex_detection: 0x followed by 8+ hex digits; 32+ contiguous hex digits (raw key/hash)

hex_redaction.method: redact_hex_id() filters hex chars, returns first 8 + '...' for strings >= 16 hex chars
hex_redaction.sha256_format: redact_sha256_colon() returns first 4 byte pairs colon-separated + '...'

artifacts_checked: manual-install: daemon binary present without install-manifest.toml
migration_detection.migration_path: remove old artifacts and reinstall via split packages
migration_detection.no_deletion: migration detection never deletes unrelated files — only reports
